key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose and design photoelectrochemical cells by quantifying where solar-to-chemical energy is lost across optical, transport, recombination, and interfacial steps.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a practical way to fit real current-voltage data, identify bottlenecks, and choose optimization strategies such as nanostructuring or co-catalyst integration.
method: Builds one framework for both BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes using physically meaningful parameters.
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency metrics, and efficiency maps under ideal and real conditions.
Decomposes measured losses and visualizes energy flow with Sankey diagrams.
evidence_signal: The model is validated against published results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, and used to compare multiple absorber material classes.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well experimental current-voltage data and model assumptions capture complex real-device interfaces and coupled loss mechanisms.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
